newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank says M3 boosted by lending in Oct.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank says M3 boosted by lending in Oct.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday that German M3 money supply growth was boosted by strong borrowing, particularly by the public sector.
In a statement, the central bank said that domestic lending in particular had boosted growth in the month.
A sharp rise in one M3 component, sight deposits, also buoyed the figure. It said the increase in these funds was probably due to money parked there ahead of the issue of Deutsche Telekom AG shares.
M3 growth overall had gained pace somewhat in the course of the month although the headline rate remained unchanged.
"After the weakening in September, growth in M3 money supply gained pace somewhat in October on a seasonally adjusted basis and on average in the month," the Bundesbank said.

It said monetary capital formation -- the process by which funds are transferred out of M3 into other forms of investment -- had grown at a six-month annualised rate of 5.2 percent up to October after 5.5 percent in September.
Lending to the private sector grew at a six-month annualised rate of 5.6 percent up to October compared to 6.3 percent in September.
